evals.prompt: im building my first commander deck (mono green, azusa) and im broke. what creatures could i run that cost 2 mana or less and are like a buck or less each? needs to actually be legal in the format
evals.expected_output: One card_search call whose q combines a format-legality operator, a creature type operator, a mana-value comparison and a USD price comparison, then an answer read off that call's payload.
expectations: At least one card_search tool call is made.
The q string of a card_search call contains a format-legality operator (f: or legal:) naming commander.
That same q string contains a card-type operator selecting creatures (t:creature or type:creature).
That same q string contains a mana-value comparison using cmc or mv with <= or < or = (for example cmc<=2).
That same q string contains a USD price comparison (usd<= or usd< , for example usd<=1).
All four constraints — format, type, mana value and price — appear together inside a single q string rather than being split across separate calls.
The transcript shows no step where the model retrieves a broad result set and then filters it itself for legality, type, mana value or price; the filtering is done by q.
The transcript contains no reply that asks the user to narrow the request instead of running a search.
